each.line: Go to, let us make brick, and burn them throughly.
Go to, let us build us a city and a tower, whose top may reach unto heaven;
and let us make us a name, lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth.
Another hundred bricks before the sun is high, and then the next hundred.
Look how the clay hardens in the fire. We can build as high as we please.
Stone is for the mountains. We have the plain, the clay and our own two hands.
Whoever carries the last brick up there will have his name remembered.
Nobody here will scatter us, because we are all of one speech and one mind.
